newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban release two French aid workers.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban release two French aid workers.

text.p: Two French aid workers held by Afghanistan's Islamic Taleban militia were released on Wednesday after a court trial in Kabul, witnesses said.
The two men, Frederic Michel and Jose Daniel Llorente, who worked for the charity Action Contre la Faim (Action Against Hunger) had been held for 26 days by the purist Taleban.

They were sentenced to one month in prison, which the court considered they had already served. Five local Afghan staff arrested with the Frenchmen were sentenced to one and a half months in jail and between nine and 29 lashes.
The Frenchmen were expected to leave Kabul for Pakistan with a delegation from the Organisation of the Islamic Conference later on Wednesday.
The seven men were arrested after a farewell party given by expatriate women aid workers for local Afghan women staff on February 21. The men denied they had attended the party.
